title: Voters in Brazil head to polls as Lula goes up against Bolsonaro's son

fullText:
Voters across Brazil have headed to the ballot boxes to decide a tightly contested presidential run-off election. The race pits the 80-year-old left-wing incumbent, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, against 45-year-old right-wing senator Flávio Bolsonaro. Lula is pursuing a fourth non-consecutive term in office, while his opponent represents the political movement of his father, former president Jair Bolsonaro, who is serving a 27-year prison term under house arrest for plotting a coup after his 2022 defeat.

The younger Bolsonaro enters the second round with considerable momentum, having finished first during the initial stage on 4 October. Historical precedent favours him, as no candidate trailing after the first round in Brazil has ever successfully overturned that deficit to secure the presidency. His campaign platform centres on reductions in public spending and taxes, alongside aggressive measures against organised crime and a commitment to free his father. He has also advocated working closely with Washington to confront powerful criminal networks.

Conversely, Lula and his Workers' Party have framed the contest as an existential fight for democratic norms, pointing to Jair Bolsonaro's coup-plotting conviction as proof that the movement threatens state institutions. Lula's camp has focused heavily on mobilising the electorate after 33 million citizens abstained during the first round. Addressing supporters on Rio de Janeiro's Copacabana beach, Lula presented the vote as a test of national sovereignty, criticising closer alignment with the United States.

The election carries major geopolitical weight, particularly regarding Brazil's relationship with Washington. While Lula has openly resisted US dominance across the Western hemisphere, relations during his tenure with Donald Trump have been strained, accompanied by accusations of US interference that American officials have denied. The outcome of the contest will fundamentally dictate whether Brazil continues under the economic and foreign policies of the traditional left or turns back to right-wing governance.

title: 7 Hilarious ‘Far Side’ Comics With the Worst Puns
description: Gary Larson’s classic comic strip, The Far Side, remains widely celebrated for its distinctive blend of high-concept humour and deliberate absurdity. Whilst the cartoonist frequently built punchlines around intricate scientific concepts or…
fullText:
Gary Larson’s classic comic strip, The Far Side, remains widely celebrated for its distinctive blend of high-concept humour and deliberate absurdity. Whilst the cartoonist frequently built punchlines around intricate scientific concepts or puzzle-like subtleties that demanded close examination, an overview of his work highlights how he equally mastered deliberately poor wordplay and lowbrow turns of phrase.

Much of this comedic impact stems from a dynamic where exceptionally bright creators write fundamentally foolish scenarios. Within The Far Side, Larson regularly turned standard idioms and familiar references upside down. These intentionally silly jokes frequently served as visual and mental palette cleansers, offering readers straightforward, delightfully foolish gags in contrast to his more complex, intellectually demanding panels.

Several prominent examples illustrate this specific brand of humour. Playing on the La Brea Tar Pits—the famed Los Angeles petroleum pools renowned for paleontological discoveries—Larson simply rhymed the geological phenomenon to create a scene depicting individuals trapped within everyday carpets. In another instance, he inverted the concept of a convenience shop into an "inconvenience store", visualising a business where essential goods were placed entirely out of customer reach.

Larson also applied this literalist wordplay to pop culture and social history. Decades after the 1940s heyday of Portuguese-born Brazilian entertainer Carmen Miranda, famed for her fruit-laden headwear, Larson introduced a bovine equivalent dubbed "Cowmen Miranda". Elsewhere, he tackled the historical American practice of printing appeals for missing and runaway children on milk cartons by depicting runaway railway trains featured on the containers instead.

The cartoonist was not uncritical of these forays into basic puns. In his retrospective collection, The Complete Far Side, Larson annotated one particular strip by describing it as his personal nominee for the worst cartoon he had ever produced, admitting that the memory still made him cringe. Nevertheless, these unabashedly simple jokes remain a notable demonstration of his versatile comedic range.

title: Claude did not invent scorpion antivenom
description: An investment research firm named Citrini Research recently partnered with artificial intelligence laboratory Anthropic to test whether an unreleased version of the Claude AI model could independently design a new drug. Citrini,…
fullText:
An investment research firm named Citrini Research recently partnered with artificial intelligence laboratory Anthropic to test whether an unreleased version of the Claude AI model could independently design a new drug. Citrini, whose staff admitted they lacked expertise in biological AI, chose to target scorpion antivenom. Conventional antivenom production is costly and difficult, frequently requiring horses to be injected with venom.

The venture began after Citrini triggered Claude's biosecurity safeguards during initial research. In response, Anthropic agreed to lift these restrictions, host Citrini at its offices, and absorb the computing and token costs, which reached just below $50,000. Anthropic is pursuing life sciences and drug development ahead of an upcoming initial public offering.

Using a 35-page prompt alongside roughly 300 subagents, Claude produced nearly 320,000 potential candidates over 64 hours. The model refined this collection down to 180 designs by removing existing proteins or recognisable toxins, and further collaborative work raised the final selection to 211 designs. Citrini subsequently spent around $150,000 to have outside laboratories, Swiss firm Adaptyv Bio and US-based Twist Biosciences, assess these designs, even though Anthropic maintains its own wet lab in California.

Laboratory evaluations revealed that 17 engineered proteins managed to bind with four of the five targeted scorpion toxins, though none bound to multiple toxins. However, binding alone does not equate to a successful medicine. Citrini confirmed that no trials had evaluated whether the proteins actually neutralised the toxins.

Independent researchers from the Technical University of Denmark highlighted that discovering binding agents is the comparatively straightforward stage of the journey. Experts warned that substantial hurdles remain regarding the proteins' bodily behaviour, stability, and safety. While Claude demonstrated a novel, autonomous identification method, the experiment generated early-stage targets rather than a functional, ready-to-use pharmaceutical treatment.

title: What is the Turkiye-Libya maritime deal, and why are the EU, Egypt opposed?
description: Libya’s eastern-based parliament has unanimously voted to ratify a controversial 2019 maritime boundary agreement with Turkiye, reversing its previous 2020 rejection of the pact. The memorandum of understanding, initially signed in Istanbul…
fullText:
Libya’s eastern-based parliament has unanimously voted to ratify a controversial 2019 maritime boundary agreement with Turkiye, reversing its previous 2020 rejection of the pact. The memorandum of understanding, initially signed in Istanbul by Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and the then-leader of the Tripoli-based Government of National Accord, maps out sea borders across the eastern Mediterranean. The arrangement grants Ankara claims across extensive, potentially gas-rich waters.

The parliamentary approval in Tobruk marks a notable realignment in Libyan regional politics. In 2020, Turkiye deployed drones and military advisers to assist the Tripoli government in repelling an assault by the eastern-based Libyan National Army, led by Khalifa Haftar. However, Ankara has spent recent years building closer ties with Haftar's command, including discussions covering Turkish defence training programmes, advanced surveillance systems, and the development of military facilities in the east.

The ratification has provoked severe international criticism. Both Egypt and the European Union swiftly dismissed the agreement as null and void. Cairo’s foreign ministry stated that the border demarcations infringe upon Egypt's exclusive economic zone and continental shelf. Meanwhile, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and European Council President Antonio Costa asserted that the memorandum violates the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, expressing complete solidarity with member states Greece and Cyprus.

Athens has briefed the United Nations Security Council, maintaining that the borders ignore Greek islands such as Crete, Karpathos, and Rhodes, while Israel has also denounced the move. The maritime dispute further complicates regional energy initiatives, notably the 2.1-billion-dollar Great Sea Interconnector, a planned subsea electricity cable intended to link Greece, Cyprus, and Israel. In response to the regional condemnation, Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan maintained that the agreement is entirely legitimate, with Ankara noting it remains outside the United Nations sea convention.

title: Trump's approval rating on economy hits all-time low as midterm looms: CNBC survey
description: Public confidence in Donald Trump's economic management has fallen to an all-time low across his two presidential terms, according to the latest CNBC All-America Economic Survey. With congressional mid-term elections approaching on…
fullText:
Public confidence in Donald Trump's economic management has fallen to an all-time low across his two presidential terms, according to the latest CNBC All-America Economic Survey. With congressional mid-term elections approaching on 3 November, eight in ten Americans now describe economic conditions as fair or poor, marking the gloomiest assessment recorded by the poll since December 2023.

The survey reveals that the president's economic approval rating has dropped to 34 per cent, whilst disapproval has climbed to 65 per cent. This results in a net rating of minus 31 percentage points, representing a nine-point decline since July. The 65 per cent disapproval figure represents the highest recorded for any administration since the tenure of Barack Obama, marginally exceeding the previous peak set under Joe Biden. Overall, Trump's broader approval remains steady but subdued, with 40 per cent approving and 59 per cent disapproving.

Widespread pessimism has expanded significantly beyond Democratic and independent voters. While 63 per cent of the broader public express negative views regarding the economic outlook, 35 per cent of Republicans now share this view. This six-point increase since July marks the highest level of internal party pessimism documented during Trump's presidencies.

These economic anxieties appear to be reshaping the electoral landscape ahead of the vote. Registered voters favour Democratic control of Congress by 52 per cent to 45 per cent, an advantage that has widened by three points since July. Across eight states featuring competitive Senate races—which Trump won by an aggregate of ten points in the 2024 presidential contest—voters now favour Democratic control by four points.

Democrats also lead on several key issues raised by voters, notably government corruption, grocery expenses, petrol prices, and democratic protection. Meanwhile, Republican polling advantages have narrowed on immigration and reversed on employment and policy regarding Iran, where public backing for military action has waned amid higher fuel costs.

title: Mass Effect Is Not Dead Yet as the Amazon Series Is Still Going Forward

fullText:
Electronic Arts has decided to shut down development studio BioWare and abandon the fifth instalment of the Mass Effect franchise. The cancellation brings an end to the next sci-fi role-playing game, which had been announced as being in early development back in 2020. Despite this major setback for the gaming property, the broader fictional universe will endure through an upcoming television adaptation produced by Amazon MGM for Prime Video.

The studio closure follows a significant change in ownership for EA, which was finalised in August 2026. The buyout placed the publisher under the control of a consortium comprising Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, Jared Kushner’s Affinity Partners, and the investment firm Silver Lake. Following the acquisition, former EA staff had warned that the new owners would pivot resources towards sports titles whilst potentially abandoning underperforming studios and properties, a prediction that has now resulted in BioWare's closure.

While the gaming branch of the franchise has halted, Amazon MGM has confirmed it is not abandoning the television adaptation, which has been in development since 2024. The creative team remains attached to the project, with Doug Jung and Daniel Casey serving as showrunners. The production team also features Mike Gamble, Karim Zreik, Ari Arad, and Jessica Jones, ensuring that television work proceeds despite the turbulence at EA.

The series will not centre on the games' original protagonist, Commander Shepard, or the Normandy crew, opting instead to introduce fresh characters within the established universe. The survival of the television show provides a vital lifeline for the intellectual property. Any future Mass Effect video games now rely entirely on whether EA chooses to sell the rights and whether an external company steps forward to purchase them. Fans now await 7 November, the traditional community celebration known as N7 Day, for potential updates regarding the television series.

Energize Lab, the manufacturer behind the artificial intelligence-enabled robot charm Eiliko, has pledged to hire an independent security firm following revelations of severe privacy and security flaws. Designed to hang on bags and interact with users via AI-powered dialogue, the device assured owners that their secrets were safe. However, security research revealed that third parties could readily access complete transcripts of conversations held with the device.

The response from Energize Lab came after more than a month of silence, during which the firm failed to answer enquiries sent to founder and chief executive Shaw Yeung. In an unsigned statement, the company apologised for the delay, citing failures to coordinate internally with its technical personnel. It confirmed the core vulnerabilities, announced a dedicated security contact address, and claimed to have rotated credentials and shut down external access to its back-end systems.

Additionally, the maker claimed to have taken offline the interface allowing remote alteration of robot responses, alongside features concerning long-term memory and bespoke user avatars. The firm promised to erase existing conversation logs, user profiles, and avatar images. Nevertheless, Energize Lab indicated that it may resume retaining personal information in the future, stating that long-term memory and custom avatar features would remain disabled only until the independent audit verifies they are secure.

Despite these assurances, significant gaps in the company's remedies remain apparent. Independent verification showed that audio recordings and customer photographs remained accessible at unsecured, publicly accessible web addresses even after the statement was issued. Security researcher Sammy Azdoufal also confirmed retaining ongoing SSH access to the devices, maintaining the ability to read transcripts and alter behaviour remotely. This ongoing exposure contradicts the firm's claim of having fully closed external access, underscoring persistent risks for consumers relying on connected companion devices.

United States President Donald Trump has called on data centre developers to reach financial settlements with local populations to secure approval for their projects. Writing on Truth Social, Trump urged firms to make deals and suggested operators pay a dividend directly to localities or individual residents. He argued that facilities facing intense local opposition quickly gain acceptance once direct financial agreements are established, describing the expansion of these sites as beneficial for the country.

The push comes as digital infrastructure becomes an increasingly contentious political topic ahead of November's midterm elections. Expanding public backlash over the environmental consequences, land requirements, and resource consumption of data hubs has led several US states to consider development moratoriums. Trump additionally asserted that he mandates large-scale sites to generate their own power and distribute or sell surplus energy to the local grid, claiming this approach would prevent electricity price increases and potentially lower costs.

Industry figures have shown openness to the broader concept of community compensation. Speaking at Nvidia’s GTC Berlin conference, Marc Boroditsky, chief revenue officer at artificial intelligence infrastructure firm Nebius, noted that the company is actively holding discussions regarding local investments. Boroditsky suggested community rewards could manifest as targeted funding for education, workforce training, and wider economic initiatives alongside existing tax contributions, describing Trump's underlying rationale as reasonable.

Securing local backing is critical as developers confront significant operational barriers. Energy availability remains a severe obstacle, with American and European electricity networks struggling under high volumes of connection requests. Chase Lochmiller, chief executive of compute infrastructure firm Crusoe, stated that securing powered land and managing local community permissions are primary operational priorities. While operators sometimes act as flexible power consumers or help finance regional grid modernisations, experts caution that the broader artificial intelligence expansion could still drive electricity bills higher.

These political interventions coincide with financial strains across the sector. Data centre shares have slipped amid anxieties over high development expenses and mounting reliance on debt markets. title: OpenAI Invests in Startup That Uses Brain Implants to Detect Cancer
description: OpenAI’s venture capital arm and Peter Thiel’s Founders Fund have invested in Coherence Neuro, a San Francisco-based startup developing brain-computer interfaces to detect and treat cancer. The backing forms part of a…
fullText:
OpenAI’s venture capital arm and Peter Thiel’s Founders Fund have invested in Coherence Neuro, a San Francisco-based startup developing brain-computer interfaces to detect and treat cancer. The backing forms part of a $45 million seed funding round for the firm, reflecting an expanding appetite among major artificial intelligence companies for ventures working with neural information.

Rather than focusing on assistive technology for paralysed individuals, Coherence is creating AI models that decode delicate electrical patterns linked to brain tumours. Having detected these signals in animal studies to track whether tumours are growing, shrinking, or returning, the startup is transitioning its work towards human clinical research. The system is also being built to administer mild electrical stimulation to stop tumour expansion, enabling the device to eventually provide automated, real-time intervention based on incoming readings.

During preliminary trials at the Royal Melbourne Hospital in Australia, researchers inserted the implant into three patients during brain tumour surgeries for about 30 minutes to evaluate safety. Coherence plans to evaluate both recording and stimulation functions in seven additional surgical patients before utilising its seed capital to initiate long-term clinical trials for people suffering from glioblastoma, a severe brain cancer. The company ultimately hopes to adapt its technology to address tumours located elsewhere in the body.

The funding round highlights a wider trend of leading AI labs supporting neurotechnology firms. Artificial intelligence is increasingly viewed as an essential tool to interpret vast volumes of raw neural data that humans cannot examine alone. OpenAI previously backed Merge Labs, an ultrasound neurotechnology firm co-founded by Sam Altman, whilst Founders Fund holds investments in Neuralink and previously supported CTRL-labs prior to its acquisition by Facebook.

Unlike OpenAI's arrangement with Merge Labs, which includes collaboration on scientific foundation models, Coherence chief executive Ben Woodington stated that OpenAI will not receive access to any health or brain data collected through the company's devices.

Severe weather is set to sweep across parts of the United Kingdom as Storm Austen approaches, prompting the Met Office to issue an amber warning for strong winds. The alert, which represents the second-highest tier of warning from the national forecaster, covers Cornwall and parts of west Devon between 03:00 and 10:00 BST on Friday.

Storm Austen is currently developing in the Atlantic and deepening as it heads towards the British Isles, driven by an upper-atmosphere jet stream reaching speeds of around 200mph. It is the first named storm of the 2026/2027 season. The low-pressure system is expected to track close to south-west England late on Thursday, bringing its most severe winds early on Friday morning before tracking through the English Channel, where it could also subject the Channel Islands to damaging conditions.

Within the amber zone, inland areas may experience wind speeds of 60 to 70mph, whilst exposed coastal stretches could face gusts of up to 80mph. Forecasters have highlighted a high probability of significant disruption, noting risks to life and injury from flying debris and sizeable coastal waves. Damage to structures, power cuts, and widespread transport delays across road and rail networks are anticipated.

A wider yellow wind warning encompasses broader swathes of southern England and south Wales, where gusts of 50 to 60mph, and up to 70mph in exposed spots, are expected. Alongside the gales, rain will spread widely, offering moisture to southern regions facing severe drought. However, southern and eastern Scotland fall under a yellow rain warning, with forecasts of 20 to 40mm widely and up to 80mm locally, raising the threat of flooding. Higher ground above 600 metres could also see snow as colder air arrives.

Looking beyond Friday, the active Atlantic jet stream will direct another unnamed deep low across the country during the weekend, potentially bringing gusts exceeding 80mph to western Scotland.

title: George Lucas's Skywalker Grill Reminds Me of Applebee's in the Best Way

fullText:
Perched on the top floor of the newly constructed, billion-dollar Lucas Museum of Narrative Art in Los Angeles, Skywalker Grill offers sweeping city views alongside an unexpected culinary vision. Founded by filmmaker George Lucas and business executive Mellody Hobson, the venue pairs a luxurious setting with an intentionally approachable, crowd-pleasing menu.

Culinary director Diego Cardoso has crafted a high-low dining selection that elevates classic comfort food. Dishes include in-house ruffled potato chips paired with spinach and artichoke dip, honey-miso glazed salmon, and Wagyu beef pigs in a blanket wrapped in puff pastry and everything-bagel seasoning. Diners can also order chicken tenders with caviar-topped ranch, alongside nostalgic items like a chicken and wild mushroom crepe inspired by the defunct Magic Pan chain. While higher-end options exist—such as a 38-dollar Wagyu burger sourced from Lucas’s Skywalker Ranch and a 52-dollar lobster salad—portions remain hearty, though certain sides like brussels sprouts and a squash pasta have proven less successful.

The restaurant's design and operational ethos emphasise broad public accessibility rather than exclusive fine dining. Resy booking guidelines invite guests to come as they are, mirroring wider museum initiatives such as free entry for minors and local residents, alongside two-dollar grilled cheese sandwiches in the lobby cafe. A widespread habit of spraying and instantly wiping kitchen surfaces often prevents cleaning sprays from working as intended. To eradicate germs successfully, disinfecting and sanitising products require a specific "dwell time" or "contact time". This requires the liquid to sit on the surface, remaining visibly wet, generally between two and ten minutes. For instance, Lysol's All-Purpose Cleaner functions as a sanitiser after ten seconds, but reaching its advertised claim of killing 99.9% of bacteria and viruses requires a full ten-minute wait, as outlined in the fine print on the reverse of the bottle.

Similarly, Clorox’s Multi-Surface Disinfecting Mist requires a ten-minute contact time to eliminate 99.9% of targeted bacteria and viruses, alongside a dedicated instruction to rinse the product completely off kitchen food-preparation areas afterwards.

Neglecting these instructions compromises hygiene in the kitchen. An artificial intelligence model developed by Anthropic has solved a 25-year-old cryptographic mystery involving the United States National Security Agency. In the late 1990s, the NSA supplied mathematical curves to the National Institute of Standards and Technology, which formally adopted them in 2000. Because the spy agency never explained how it generated the initial seed numbers, researchers long suspected that the curves contained an intentional backdoor designed for surveillance.

Suspicion heightened following revelations leaked by Edward Snowden, which showed the NSA had previously sought to undermine cryptographic standards, prompting NIST to drop another compromised tool known as Dual EC. For decades, cryptographers examined the mysterious seeds, pursuing leads such as a forgotten phrase supposedly used by late NSA mathematician Jerry Solinas. Security researchers attempted public records requests, and in 2023, a bounty exceeding $12,000—rising past $36,000 for charity—was established to uncover the true origin of the numbers.

Tasked with the problem without being told earlier theories, an internal Anthropic research model took under 30 minutes to deduce the answer. The AI determined that five NIST curve seeds originated from lrand48, an ordinary random-number generator commonly found in older C programming libraries, combined with timestamps from 1997 and 1998. The model accurately recreated the sequence behind the widely adopted P-256 curve, matching its seed on the 1,842nd candidate.

Anthropic noted that this predictable origin makes a hidden backdoor far less probable, although questions remain regarding why certain candidates were skipped. Crucially, Bitcoin was never reliant on these contested parameters. Bitcoin wallets use an alternative elliptic curve called secp256k1, chosen by creator Satoshi Nakamoto and later adopted by Ethereum and Bitcoin's 2021 Taproot upgrade. Unlike P-256's seed-derived 77-digit figure, secp256k1 relies on two small, fixed numbers, offering virtually no leeway to insert backdoors. However, this breakthrough does not shield cryptocurrency networks from future quantum computers, which remain capable of calculating secret keys directly from public keys on the blockchain.

Citric acid comes as a dry, food-safe powder that is easy to store in bulk, produces a much milder odour than vinegar, and offers modest antibacterial qualities, even though it is not a complete disinfectant.

To prepare the mixture, the powder is dissolved into water until the crystals disappear. While ordinary tap water works in a pinch, distilled water is the superior choice because it is completely devoid of minerals. Adding extra citric acid simply increases the potency of the cleaner. Users must, however, wear washing-up gloves during application, as the acidic liquid can cause irritation to delicate skin.

The resulting liquid works according to manufacturer guidelines for internal machine maintenance, but it also cleans neglected external areas. Mineral rings around tap bases can be cleared by applying the solution directly or placing a saturated paper towel over the spot before wiping it clean. Unlike typical generative systems, Jev is not a large language model, although it is built upon a transformer architecture. Rather than generating text or computer code, the system calculates probabilities that the startup describes as calibrated decisions. TypeSafe claims this operational framework allows the model to function substantially faster while consuming far fewer tokens than conventional text-based alternatives.

The underlying rationale centres on repurposing AI capabilities specifically for automated workflows. title: NBA commissioner Adam Silver says league could introduce ‘smart ball’ technology as soon as next year
description: The National Basketball Association could introduce a high-tech "smart ball" into official games as soon as next year. Speaking in an interview with CNBC, NBA Commissioner Adam Silver revealed that the league…
fullText:
The National Basketball Association could introduce a high-tech "smart ball" into official games as soon as next year. Speaking in an interview with CNBC, NBA Commissioner Adam Silver revealed that the league is collaborating with basketball manufacturer Wilson to develop a ball containing a microchip Bluetooth sensor. This internal device tracks motion, rotation, and shifts in trajectory, potentially reshaping how games are refereed.

Weighing roughly one gram, the sensor makes up only a tiny fraction of a standard 620-gram basketball. Trials have already taken place across the NBA G League, the Summer League, and selected preseason fixtures, where participants used both traditional and sensor-equipped balls. According to Silver, players could not tell the difference between the two, meeting the league's aim of preserving the authentic feel and bounce of the equipment.

The most pressing role for the innovation is on-court officiating. Referees could use the data to determine whether an athlete touched the ball prior to it crossing the boundary line by monitoring slight adjustments in spin. The technology could also detect whether a shot's path was altered. Looking further ahead, Silver noted that a consumer model could arrive in a few years, offering everyday players data on shooting mechanics, angles, and ball rotation.

At the same time, the league is exploring broader technological integrations, including in-game wearable devices. Referees recently conducted a successful pilot using wrist wearables during selected preseason and Summer League fixtures to communicate with the replay centre regarding clock issues, reviews, and score adjustments, though this trial will not continue into the regular season.

Introducing player wearables into competitive matches remains unresolved. Although athletes regularly monitor their health off the court, formal talks between the league and the National Basketball Players Association are ongoing. Silver acknowledged player concerns that in-game physical performance data could be leveraged against them during contract negotiations if it revealed signs of decline.

title: How to use the parental controls on iOS 27
description: Following the release of its September operating system updates, Apple has overhauled its Screen Time parental controls across its ecosystem. Developed alongside the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP), the refreshed features aim…
fullText:
Following the release of its September operating system updates, Apple has overhauled its Screen Time parental controls across its ecosystem. Developed alongside the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP), the refreshed features aim to help guardians balance their children’s digital engagement with schoolwork, physical activity, sleep, and family commitments. The initiative also includes an official companion guide titled Building Healthy Digital Habits to support families with ongoing guidance.

The updated system replaces traditional App Limits with more flexible Time Allowances. Rather than setting individual timers on dozens of specific applications, guardians can establish broader daily limits and distribute hours across specific groupings such as social media, gaming, or entertainment, as well as bespoke custom categories. Setting up a child’s profile has also been streamlined, serving age-tailored app suggestions instead of installing every default programme across the home screen.

Safety protections across Apple’s communication and browsing tools have seen substantial upgrades. A new Ask to Browse setting requires young users to seek approval via Messages before visiting unapproved websites on Safari, whilst Ask to Add Contacts mandates parental sign-off before a child can call or message unfamiliar phone numbers. Furthermore, Communication Safety has been expanded beyond nudity detection to identify and blur scenes of graphic violence and gore across FaceTime, AirDrop, and Messages. Parents can also temporarily lock a child's screen instantly using a new Pause Device function.

To access the refreshed Screen Time tools, households must ensure every iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, and Apple TV in their Family Sharing group runs its respective version 27 operating system. Devices unable to upgrade will remain on legacy software, which creates an operational gap across older hardware. Initial setups apply stricter defaults, including automatic web and contact approvals for users under 13, alongside universal content blurring for all minors under 18.

title: Trump’s attempt to rename AI is looking awfully artificial

fullText:
United States President Donald Trump has launched a concerted effort to rebrand artificial intelligence across the federal government, insisting that the sector instead be known as "super intelligence". Following an address at the United Nations last month where he claimed the word "artificial" makes the technology sound fake, Trump signed an executive order barring the use of "AI" wherever possible. He subsequently escalated the rhetoric, warning that the White House regards anyone still using the term artificial intelligence as "THE ENEMY".

The administration's linguistic mandate has triggered rapid revisions across government bodies. The US Center for AI Standards and Innovation has been retitled the Center for Advancing Innovation and Standards for Super Intelligence. Additionally, the Department of Justice has altered its communication materials, recently retroactively classifying a long-running streaming fraud scheme as "Super Intelligence-Assisted Music Streaming Fraud".

Prominent leaders across the technology sector have largely fallen in line with the decree. Elon Musk committed to changing the name of SpaceXAI to SpaceXSI, whilst Jeff Bezos voiced support, noting that the word artificial is unflattering. Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang and OpenAI leader Sam Altman have similarly endorsed the shift, although Altman confirmed that OpenAI would not alter its corporate moniker. Concurrently, Trump has begun utilising "artificial" as a broader slur, retiring the phrase "fake news media" to brand the press "artificial media".

This state-mandated shift matters because it artificially blurs critical technical distinctions within computer science. Historically, the single word "superintelligence" specifically described hypothetical, highly advanced systems capable of exceeding human cognitive capabilities, rather than commonplace automation or music-generation tools. Applying the term universally dilutes the marketing power of future breakthroughs. Furthermore, Trump faces hurdles across other government branches, as he cannot stop Congress from using the original phrase, which remains codified in existing federal statutes that government agencies must uphold in court.

title: Five people shot and killed in apparent murder-suicide, Georgia police say

fullText:
Five members of the same family have died following a suspected murder-suicide at a residence in Douglas, south Georgia. Emergency services attended the property on Friday after receiving an active shooter alert, which had been placed by one of the victims.

Upon entering the house, police discovered the bodies of four adults who had sustained fatal gunshot wounds. A fifth person was taken to a local hospital for emergency treatment, but was subsequently pronounced dead. Authorities have not yet disclosed the precise sequence of events or identified who among the household fired the shots, noting that the broader circumstances remain under formal investigation.

Law enforcement revealed that an earlier emergency call had been logged from the residence hours before the fatal gunfire took place. During that prior contact, a woman residing at the address reported to police that her husband’s smoking was killing her. Following that initial complaint, emergency medical staff conveyed the woman to a nearby medical centre.

Speaking at a media conference on Saturday, Douglas Police Chief Brannen Pruette acknowledged the deep distress the deaths have caused within the local community, appealing to the public to afford the surviving relatives privacy whilst they mourn. Police have kept further operational findings confidential as inquiries into the case proceed.

The event marks the second apparent murder-suicide in the area within a span of three months, according to Douglas City Manager Charlie Davis. Addressing the broader context of the incident, Davis highlighted the pervasive nature of domestic violence, remarking that it transcends race, religion, and geographic location. He urged residents to avoid unverified speculation surrounding the tragedy, which coincided with another lethal family shooting and suicide reported in Pennsylvania on the same day.
